# Ouro UI

> A kit for agents to build interfaces people enjoy and other agents can use, on the web, Apple, Windows and Android.[^native] MIT.[^glance-licence] Components per platform: web, every item under Items below; Apple 20,[^glance-apple] Windows 26[^glance-windows] and Android 26.[^glance-android] Which ones, including chat: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/platforms/parity/

- Ouro HX (human experience): components. Web: copy-in source from a shadcn registry, start at https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/agent-quickstart.md. Apple: Swift package, start at https://ui.ouroboros.bot/apple/start/. Windows: WinUI 3,[^glance-windows] start at https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/platforms/windows/. Android: Compose, start at https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/platforms/android/. Ouro Current keeps all four up to date with one pull request per release.[^open-current]
- Ouro AX (agent experience): the doors agents use (CLIs, HTTP APIs, MCP servers, App Intents, AppFunctions, Windows App Actions), with a kit and an AX X-ray. Guide: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax.md
- Actions: declare an action once to generate its button and its agent tools; existing MCP tools keep their names and inputs.[^open-actions] Each is a read, a write, consequential (the person confirms first) or person-only (no agent door offers it).[^person-only]
- Composed UI: an agent sends a card as data, checked against your app's catalog and drawn by each kit.[^composed] Sends cards to any MCP Apps host; reads A2UI.[^composed] Guide: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/composed-ui.md
- Missing a component? Write it natively beside Ouro's and offer it back as a pull request.
- Check your work: Ouro check (node scripts/ouro/check/check.ts <built folder>) finds what's broken on every page; HX X-ray names every component on a page; AX X-ray tests every door.[^open-xray]

Evidence (10 models, scored on app state): through Ouro's actions agents finished 98% of jobs and paid without the person 0 of 32 times; driving the browser, 83% and 30 of 30.[^open-benchmark] Method and every run, with where every number comes from:[^open-runs] https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/agent-interfaces/

## Common needs

The full item list, under Items below, is long. These are the items for needs apps often have; read one's page at https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/<item>.md.

- Dark mode: `color-scheme-toggle`, with `ColorSchemeProvider` from `@/lib/ouro/color-scheme` around the app (https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/color-scheme-provider.md); for a plain on/off, a `switch` with `useColorScheme()` (https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/use-color-scheme.md).
- A form that validates: `form` with `text-field`, `select`, `switch`, `checkbox`; errors from your own `onSubmit` or from a server action.
- Asking before a destructive action: `confirm-dialog`. Other dialogs: `dialog`; a panel from the edge: `sheet`; editing in a panel that saves and closes: `edit-sheet`.
- Saying something happened: `toaster`. A message on the page: `alert`. Nothing here yet: `moment`. Loading: `skeleton`, `spinner`.
- Getting around: `navbar`, `sidebar`, `tabs`, `menu`, `command` (a command palette).
- Data: `table`, `combobox`, `date-picker`.
- A design system's tokens and theme: ouro-base adds the `--ouro-*` tokens once per app, and ouro-theme is an optional shadcn theme (https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/installing.md).
- Interfaces an agent sends: Ouro's own tree, which can travel as A2UI messages or in an MCP Apps view; see https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/composed-ui.md.

## Ouro HX for web

Designed down to the last tap and the last prop. Interactions that feel right to the humans using them. Code that's obvious to the agents building with them. Copy-in source distributed as a shadcn/ui registry on GitHub (ourostack/ouro-ui). It is not an npm package: the shadcn CLI copies the components you add into your app.

At a glance:

- Licence: MIT (LICENSE), copyright Ari Mendelow.[^glance-licence]
- Native kits, no Flutter or React Native on purpose:[^native] web (React, here: the catalog below); Apple (SwiftUI, https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-apple), 20 components;[^glance-apple] Windows (WinUI 3, https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-windows) and Android (Compose, https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-android), 26 (Windows) and 26 (Android) of core's components,[^glance-windows][^glance-android] Android on CI emulators, not a real device.[^android-first]
- States: a field's error is one prop that shows the error and marks the control,[^states-prop] and Ouro check opens your built pages and the states you list, and reports the ones it can decide are broken: the floor, not proof a person gets through them.[^states-check]
- Accessibility: every story passes axe.[^glance-axe] VoiceOver and NVDA read the components on every released commit, right after its tag, and a commit that breaks them is reverted and the revert released.[^glance-sr]
- Open questions: outside audit (https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui/issues/2315); Android on real devices (https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui/issues/2294).[^glance-open]

Building a settings page, a dashboard or a list beside its detail? Install its page pattern, a whole page the theme draws, then change it: npx shadcn@latest add @ouro/ouro-base @ouro/settings-page --yes (or dashboard-page, list-detail-page), after the quickstart's step 3. A page is done when it builds and Ouro check passes. Guide: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/patterns.md

Building a new app? Start at https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/agent-quickstart.md: five steps, every file whole, for a new Vite app with a validated form, a light and dark toggle and a confirmation dialog.[^quickstart]

Ouro UI is a complete kit for agents to build delightful interfaces for people and other agents. An agent composes an interface as data in Ouro's own tree, validated against the app's catalog, and every kit draws it natively; each button is an action declared once, which a person presses and an agent calls as a tool, with consent built in and an X-ray to check both[^composed]: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/composed-ui.md Core's generator turns one action declaration into a CLI command, MCP and WebMCP tools, a web control, an App Intent, a SwiftUI button and a Reins action.[^one-action] A consequential action asks the person to confirm what an agent prepared before it runs.[^consent-confirm] A person-only action has no agent door; each door answers an agent with a typed refusal.[^person-only] MCP Apps (https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps) and A2UI (https://a2ui.org/) are formats of that tree:[^works-with] an MCP tool result carries it, then only what changed, to an MCP Apps view,[^mcp-app] and the A2UI adapter turns A2UI messages into it.[^a2ui-render] Agent benchmark: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/agent-interfaces.md. Model reviews: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/model-reviews/.

Ouro HX for web is this repository's part of Ouro UI: the components for the screens people use, on the web. Ouro AX ("Ouro AX" below) is for the doors agents use.

Check what you build first: build your app, run node scripts/ouro/check/check.ts <built folder> (from the ouro-check item: npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/ouro-check#v1.3.558) and fix what it reports. It installs under scripts/ouro/, outside your TypeScript project, so tsc -b skips it. It imports the Ouro AX kit as #ouro-ax/<file>: npm pkg set "imports.#ouro-ax/*=./src/lib/ouro/ax/*" adds that once (src/lib is your lib folder). It opens your pages at screen sizes from a phone to a wide desktop, light and dark, and finds overlap, sideways scroll, clipped text, blurry pictures and serious axe-core violations, narrow text (prose a max-width holds well short of its column), and long lines only where you declare a measure.[^check] Long lines are opt-in, because a fixed text measure is a design choice.[^long-lines] Declare one in ouro-check.json only where your design or the request sets it, and don't cap text width just to quiet the check. A clean report is the floor: what measurement can decide isn't broken. It doesn't show that people understand the screen; before you call a screen good, watch a few people do its task.[^floor] Guide: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/guardrails.md

Ask of every pixel, control, command, flag and line of output whether the people who made the Mac and the iPhone would ship it. Start from the jobs people do, not a reference product's items, and let each element earn its place. Before a person sees a screen, a mock or a capture of either, pass the beauty gate: put it beside its references, ask independent critics, and fix until they approve. Before agents rely on a door, pass the AX gate: fresh agents do real jobs with only the door, then independent critics read the transcripts (https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/design-craft.md).

## Install

In an existing Vite or Next.js app with Tailwind CSS v4[^tailwind-4] and an "@/*" path alias, run shadcn init once, with the Base UI base and without -t/--template, register the @ouro namespace, then add items. The namespace serves the newest release (the same code as #v1.3.558)[^namespace] and installs much faster than the GitHub addresses, which fetch each file from GitHub:

```sh
npx shadcn@latest init --base base --preset nova --yes --no-monorepo
# Register @ouro in components.json:
node -e "const fs=require('fs');const c=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('components.json','utf8'));c.registries={'@ouro':'https://ui.ouroboros.bot/r/{name}.json'};fs.writeFileSync('components.json',JSON.stringify(c,null,2))"
# ouro-base first, once per app: the tokens every component needs. Then the components.
npx shadcn@latest add @ouro/ouro-base @ouro/dialog @ouro/form --yes
```

To pin a release instead, use the GitHub addresses:

```sh
npx shadcn@latest search 'ourostack/ouro-ui#v1.3.558'      # list the items
npx shadcn@latest view 'ourostack/ouro-ui/dialog#v1.3.558'  # read one item
npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/ouro-base#v1.3.558
npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/dialog#v1.3.558     # install a component
```

- Add ouro-base once, before the first component. No component installs it, so no later add changes the app's stylesheet (in v0.7.0 every component still installs it, and an add can rewrite the stylesheet).[^ouro-base-only][^v0.7.0] Without it, overlays have no backdrop or motion and fields no border, and in development the first component to mount logs the command to run.[^theme-check]

- Starting from nothing? Set up a new Vite or Next.js app first: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/installing.md#start-a-new-app
- A new Vite app needs @tailwindcss/vite, @import "tailwindcss";, a Vite @ alias, and "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] } in both tsconfig.json and tsconfig.app.json (no baseUrl on TypeScript 6 or 7) before init: shadcn reads the root file, and tsc -b builds the app one.[^vite-app]
- --preset nova lets init run without prompts. It sets shadcn's starting theme, font and icons, which Ouro components read like any shadcn theme. The install test runs nova and vega; other presets are untested.
- A GitHub source is owner/repo#ref; an item is owner/repo/item#ref. @v1.3.558, github: and /tree/ URLs do not work.
- A release tag (#v1.3.558) installs the item and every Ouro dependency at that tag.[^release-pins] Every install needs a release tag or @ouro: main has no registry.json, so an address without a ref fails with "did not return a root registry.json file".[^main-no-registry]
- Components land in components/ouro/<component>/ and the helpers they import in lib/ouro/, one file each.[^lands] Ouro UI never writes to components/ui/, so do not pass --overwrite on a first install.[^not-ui]
- Tests are optional: add <item>-tests beside the item (npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/dialog#v1.3.558 ourostack/ouro-ui/dialog-tests#v1.3.558), or ouro-tests for all of them.[^ouro-tests] They need Vitest 4.1.11 or later in browser mode, Playwright 1.58.1 or later, axe-core 4.13.0 or later and Storybook 10.2.10 or later, and never change a version the app already has (v0.7.0's items still carry versions: after add, restore the versions you had pinned).[^minimums][^v0.7.0] Ouro UI's own CI runs them on Vitest 5 only; Vitest 4 is the stated minimum, not a tested one.[^vitest-5][^minimums] The ouro-testing install message lists the config files to add.

## Changing a component

The components you add are yours to change. When to send a change back to Ouro UI: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/installing.md#changing-a-component

## Ouro AX

Ouro AX is the part of Ouro UI for agents: it is for the interfaces an agent uses, such as a CLI, an HTTP API or an MCP server, as Ouro HX is for the screens a person uses. Its parts:

- A standard with an X-ray: `ax-claims` holds the standard as checkable claims about agent-facing surfaces. `ax-xray` calls an interface from outside, the way an agent would, and reports which claims hold on which command, route and tool, with the fix where one does not.
- A kit: with `ax-command`, one definition of a command gives its parser, its help and `help --json`, `--json` output, exit codes, one-line errors that name the fix, and the same command as an MCP tool. An action returns a typed outcome (`ax-outcome`), a wait returns a typed wait with a cursor (`ax-wait`), and `ax-work-event` records who acted for whom.
- The evaluation gate: a claim is `must` only when an agent evaluation shows agents failing without it, or when it guards against a stated safety, compatibility or integrity hazard.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/ouro-ax#v1.3.558         # the kit and the X-ray, in lib/ouro/ax/ and scripts/ouro/ax/
npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/ouro-ax-tests#v1.3.558   # with their node:test tests
```

Its Node-only parts (the X-ray, the flow runner, the surfaces check and their tests) install under scripts/ouro/ax/, outside your TypeScript project, so tsc -b does not read them. They import the kit as #ouro-ax/<file>: npm pkg set "imports.#ouro-ax/*=./src/lib/ouro/ax/*" adds that once.

The guide: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax.md. A morning with an agent, with the kit's example tool running in your browser: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/ax/

## Ouro UI for Apple

Ouro HX and Ouro AX in Swift, for iPhone, iPad and Mac (ourostack/ouro-ui-apple): https://ui.ouroboros.bot/apple/. The section's parts:

- Ouro HX (the components, the spring and the haptics): since 1.4.0 every corner is a squircle, and OuroCheckbox's box fills and its tick draws along its path, as web Ouro's does.[^hx-1-4] OuroCheckboxMark and OuroCheckboxPressStyle draw the same box in your own rows.[^hx-1-4] Since 1.5.0, `.ouroAction(light:dark:)` gives solid primary buttons the app's own main-action colours, as web's `--ouro-action` does.[^hx-1-5] https://ui.ouroboros.bot/apple/hx/
- The App Intents X-ray (claims held): reads a built app's App Intents from outside and checks them against Ouro AX for Apple's claims. https://ui.ouroboros.bot/apple/ax/
- Ouro Reins (behaviour): an agent reads the app's screens as state and actions and drives it with `ls` and `do`, headless, from fixtures, with the network blocked. Spoonjoy's Kitchen-to-cook-mode journey ran in a median 18.7 ms this way against 16.7 s through XCUITest.[^reins-timing] The idea is Shopify's Reflex (https://shopify.engineering/reflex). Its wire contract is a spec of its own, docs/ouro-reins/PROTOCOL.md in ouro-ui-apple, and a second driver speaks it for any app on a Mac, from the app's tree of controls or a screenshot's text.[^reins-protocol] https://ui.ouroboros.bot/apple/reins/
- Ouro Feel (how it feels): checks jank genre by genre from a UI test: the way back, overlay dismissal, inside the window, tap landing (with an absolute bar for rapid double taps), double-draw, jump after landing, late or lingering chrome, snap with no transition, settle time and place stability.[^feel-genres] https://ui.ouroboros.bot/apple/feel/
- OuroA2UI (agent-composed UI, new in 0.5.0): draws Ouro HX's A2UI catalog in SwiftUI, where every button is one of the app's declared actions and follows its consent class.[^a2ui] Since 1.1.0 the catalog also takes fields (`TextField`, `Checkbox` and `Select`), and `ComposedTree` draws a tree that didn't come as A2UI.[^a2ui-1-1] https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-apple/blob/bf029bd61a076fdcdd0c014bb333cd654f08129e/README.md#agent-composed-ui-a2ui

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-apple.git", from: "1.10.1")   // the foundations, the X-ray, Feel, Reins and OuroA2UI
```

Ouro Feel and Ouro Reins shipped in ouro-ui-apple 0.4.1 as the OuroFeel and OuroReins products.[^feel-reins] Their guides are docs/ouro-feel/README.md and docs/ouro-reins/README.md in that repository.

## Items

- `ouro-base`: Add it once per app, before your first component; no component installs it, so later adds never touch your stylesheet. What every Ouro UI component needs in the app's CSS: success and warning colors, a destructive foreground, the field border color (--input) and --radius when your theme has none, the motion tokens, the press utility, the keyframes for spinners, progress bars and skeletons, and --ouro-layer, the z-index of sheets and dialogs (50; raise it in a :root rule of your own if your app has fixed bars above z-50).
- `ouro-plain`: Ouro UI's states as classes, for markup that is not an Ouro component, such as rows and controls a page builds as strings or prerenders to read without a script: the focus ring, a linked row, a disclosure, a skip link, actions shown on hover or focus, current links, toggles, segmented choices and options. Add it once, after ouro-base, only if your app has such markup.
- `ouro-theme`: Ouro UI's own look, as a shadcn theme for :root and .dark. Skip it to keep your app's theme.
- `ouro-lib`: Every helper in lib/ouro in one item. You don't need to add it: each component installs only the helpers it imports (the lib-<name> items).
- `ouro-testing`: Installed with every -tests item; you don't need to add it. The test kit Ouro UI's tests use: Vitest browser projects with the drag, flick, tap, doubleTap, touchDrag, touchStep, pointerPress, emulateMedia, pageZoom, resetPageZoom, setPageZoom and restoreTouch commands, the rotate helper (which turns the phone viewport and resets Chromium's zoom; the ouro-touch project fails a test that leaves the page zoomed), the act helper, the holdFrames helper (which holds animation frames and the clock still so a test steps a spring itself), the motion helpers (expectMotion, expectNoMotion, expectGestureSettle, expectTransition and parseDuration, which prove exactly which CSS properties a state change runs on each part), watchAnnouncements (which records what live regions announce, so a test proves a message is heard once per change), axeExclude, and the end-to-end story helper.
- `button`: A button, or a link styled as one. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/button.md
- `text`: Body text in the theme's type scale and colors. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/text.md
- `heading`: A section title, `<h1>` to `<h6>`, in the theme's foreground color. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/heading.md
- `sheet`: A panel that slides in from an edge and is dragged back to dismiss: the mobile form of a dialog. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/sheet.md
- `dialog`: A dialog that presents itself for the screen: a centered dialog on wider screens and a bottom sheet you can drag away on phones (below 640px). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/dialog.md
- `confirm-dialog`: Asks the user to confirm an action, with Cancel focused first. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/confirm-dialog.md
- `field`: A labeled form control: the label, an optional description, the control and its error, wired together with ids that match between the server and the browser. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/field.md
- `fieldset`: A titled group of related fields, such as an address, rendered as a `<fieldset>` named by its legend. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/fieldset.md
- `link`: A text link that navigates through your router. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/link.md
- `text-field`: A labeled one-line text input on the Field contract: pass `label`, and `error` from your server action or client check. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/text-field.md
- `text-area`: A labeled multi-line text field on the Field contract, a native `<textarea>`: pass `label`, and `error` from your server action or client check. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/text-area.md
- `checkbox`: A labeled checkbox on the Field contract, with the label to its right: pass `label`, and `checked` with `onCheckedChange` (or `defaultChecked`). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/checkbox.md
- `checkbox-group`: A group of checkboxes under one legend, on the Field contract, for picking any number of choices: pass `legend`, and `options` (or `Checkbox` children). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/checkbox-group.md
- `radio-group`: A group of radios under one legend, on the Field contract, for picking exactly one choice: pass `legend`, and `options` (or `Radio` children). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/radio-group.md
- `switch`: A labeled on/off switch on the Field contract, with the label to its right: pass `label`, and `checked` with `onCheckedChange` (or `defaultChecked`). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/switch.md
- `form`: A form that validates with the browser's own constraints (`required`, `type="email"`, `pattern`) and shows server errors on the matching fields. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/form.md
- `edit-sheet`: Edits something in a form inside a dialog: the whole interaction, done right. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/edit-sheet.md
- `select`: A labeled list of choices on the Field contract: pass `label`, `options` (or `SelectItem` children) and `error` from your server action or client check. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/select.md
- `native-select`: A labeled native `<select>` on the Field contract: pass `label`, `options` (or `<option>` children) and `error`. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/native-select.md
- `number-field`: A labeled number input on the Field contract: pass `label`, and `error` from your server action or client check. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/number-field.md
- `slider`: A labeled slider on the Field contract: pass `label`, and a `defaultValue` (or `value` with `onValueChange`). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/slider.md
- `combobox`: A text input that filters a list of items as people type, on the Field contract: pass `label`, `items`, and `error` from your server action or client check. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/combobox.md
- `toaster`: Shows the toasts you send with `toast("Saved")` from `@/lib/ouro/toast`: render it once, at the root of your app, inside `OuroProvider` if you use one, or alone. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/toaster.md
- `spinner`: A small spinning ring that says an action is under way, inline: in a field's adornment, a toast's or a menu entry's icon, or beside the words that say what is happening. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/spinner.md
- `progress`: A bar that shows how far along a task is, or that it is under way when you can't tell. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/progress.md
- `skeleton`: A placeholder that breathes after a second in the shape and size of content that is still loading, so the content takes its place without moving anything. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/skeleton.md
- `avatar`: A person's picture, or their initials until it loads or when it fails, in a color picked from the name. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/avatar.md
- `badge`: A short label for a status, category or count: "Draft", "Vegan", "3". Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/badge.md
- `alert`: An inline message in the page: something saved, something failed, something to know before going on. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/alert.md
- `separator`: A thin line in the theme's border color between groups of content, horizontal or vertical. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/separator.md
- `kbd`: A keyboard shortcut, in the reader's platform's notation: `keys={["mod", "k"]}` shows ⌘K on a Mac, iPhone or iPad and Ctrl+K elsewhere. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/kbd.md
- `popover`: A small panel beside its trigger, for a short form or a few choices: a share link, filters, a quick edit. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/popover.md
- `tooltip`: A short label that appears beside its trigger on hover and keyboard focus, for an icon button's purpose or a control's shortcut. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/tooltip.md
- `hover-card`: A preview of where a link goes, shown when a mouse rests on the link or the keyboard focuses it: a cook's profile, a recipe's summary. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/hover-card.md
- `menu`: A list of actions that opens from a button, from a right-click or long press, or from a menubar, with one API for all three. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/menu.md
- `command`: A command palette: a searchable list of every action in the app, in a dialog. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/command.md
- `tabs`: Tabs that switch between panels in place: an accessible tab list with roving focus, arrow-key navigation, a line that slides to the selected tab, and 44px tabs on touch screens. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/tabs.md
- `segmented-control`: An iOS-style segmented control: a row of equal segments with a raised thumb that slides to the checked one, for switching how one view shows its content in place, such as list or grid. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/segmented-control.md
- `accordion`: A stack of titles that each open their own content, for FAQs and long settings pages. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/accordion.md
- `collapsible`: One section that opens and closes under its title, such as nutrition facts under a recipe. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/collapsible.md
- `show-more`: "Show more" for a long list or a long text. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/show-more.md
- `card`: A surface that groups one thing's content: a media slot across the top, a title with a description and an action, a body, and a footer. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/card.md
- `item`: One row of a list: leading media, a title with a description, and trailing actions. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/item.md
- `item-group`: A list of `Item` rows, with an optional label that names it, lines between the rows, and what to show when it is empty. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/item-group.md
- `empty`: What a list, search or page shows when it has nothing in it: an icon, a title that says what is empty, a sentence on what to do, and the action that does it. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/empty.md
- `scroll-area`: A scrolling region with a thin scrollbar in the theme's color, inside a height you set. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/scroll-area.md
- `aspect-ratio`: A frame that keeps an image, video or map at a fixed shape while its width follows the layout, so the page does not jump when the media loads. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/aspect-ratio.md
- `stack`: Lays its children out top to bottom with an even gap. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/stack.md
- `row`: Lays its children out side by side with an even gap, centered up and down. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/row.md
- `navbar`: The bar across the top of an app: your brand, the main links and a few controls, with the current page marked `aria-current="page"`, and the link of the section it is in `aria-current="true"`, both underlined in the primary colour, distinct from hover and press highlights. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/navbar.md
- `sidebar`: The column of links down the side of an app, in sections, with the current page marked `aria-current="page"` and a bar at the start edge, distinct from hover and press highlights. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/sidebar.md
- `sidebar-layout`: The shell of an app with a `Sidebar`: the sidebar beside the page from 640px up, in view while the page scrolls, and a sticky top bar with the sidebar's menu button below 640px. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/sidebar-layout.md
- `stacked-layout`: The shell of an app with a `Navbar`: the bar across the top, in view while the page scrolls, an optional `toolbar` under it for the page's own tools, and the page below them in a centered column. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/stacked-layout.md
- `auth-layout`: The page for signing in, signing up or resetting a password: one `Card` in the middle of the screen, with your brand, the title as the page's `<h1>`, the form, and a line under the card. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/auth-layout.md
- `breadcrumb`: The trail from the top of the site to the current page: a labelled `<nav>` with an ordered list of links, the last item marked `aria-current="page"`. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/breadcrumb.md
- `pagination`: Page navigation for a long list: Previous, the page numbers with gaps, and Next, with the current page marked `aria-current="page"`. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/pagination.md
- `navigation-menu`: A row of links where some open a panel of further links, each with a line of description: the navigation of a site with more pages than fit in a bar. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/navigation-menu.md
- `table`: A data table: a caption, column headers, and rows, from `columns` and `rows` or from parts. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/table.md
- `description-list`: One thing's details as pairs of a term and its value: a recipe's prep time and servings, an order's date and total, an account's email. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/description-list.md
- `toggle`: A button that stays pressed until it is pressed again, such as Bold in a text toolbar. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/toggle.md
- `toggle-group`: A row of related toggles that share one value, such as text alignment or bold, italic and underline in a toolbar. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/toggle-group.md
- `button-group`: Related buttons joined into one control, such as Previous, a page number and Next, or a split button. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/button-group.md
- `otp-field`: A one-time code entry on the Field contract: one slot per character, with focus that moves as the person types, a whole code pasted at once, and `autoComplete="one-time-code"` so phones offer the code from a text message. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/otp-field.md
- `file-field`: A labeled file input with a drop zone, on the Field contract. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/file-field.md
- `color-field`: A color on the Field contract: a swatch that opens the system color picker, next to the same color as hex text, kept in step both ways. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/color-field.md
- `swipe-actions`: A list row with actions beside it that a horizontal swipe reveals: swipe toward the start for the `trailing` actions (Delete, Archive), toward the end for the `leading` ones (Pin). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/swipe-actions.md
- `reorderable`: A list the user puts in order: recipe steps, a queue, favorites. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/reorderable.md
- `calendar`: A month grid to pick a day or a range of days, with the arrow keys or a press. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/calendar.md
- `date-picker`: A labeled date field. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/date-picker.md
- `carousel`: A row of slides the user swipes or steps through with Previous and Next buttons: recipe photos, a few featured cards. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/carousel.md
- `resizable`: Panels side by side (or stacked) with a draggable handle between each pair: a file list beside an editor, a preview above a console. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/resizable.md
- `chart`: A chart drawn in the theme's colors, which people can use without seeing it: a figure named by its `title`, a summary for screen readers, and a table of every value (visible with `showTable`). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/chart.md
- `message`: One message in a chat: who wrote it, their avatar and what they wrote, with any attachments under it. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/message.md
- `message-list`: A conversation: `Message`s in a scrolling, labeled region that opens at the newest one. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/message-list.md
- `attachment`: A file attached to a chat message, or waiting to be sent with one: an icon for its kind, its name and size. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/attachment.md
- `thread-summary`: The line under a post that leads to its thread: who replied, "N replies" (a button that opens the thread) and when the last reply came. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/thread-summary.md
- `checklist`: A list of things to tick off, such as a recipe's ingredients or a shopping list: each row a checkbox the whole row toggles, with an optional value and action. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/checklist.md
- `inspector`: X-ray for a page built with Ouro HX: outlines every Ouro component on the page with its name, linked to its docs, and lists them all for keyboard and screen reader users. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/inspector.md
- `skip-link`: The "Skip to main content" link a keyboard or screen-reader user meets first on every page, so one Tab and Enter jump past the header and navigation. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/skip-link.md
- `tab-bar`: The bar of tabs at the bottom of a phone screen: two to five of the app's top-level pages, each an icon over a short label, with the current page marked `aria-current="page"` and an accent wash. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/tab-bar.md
- `route-progress`: The thin bar across the top of the screen while the app loads the next page or submits a form, so a click that waits on the server never feels frozen: one global affordance instead of a pending state on every action. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/route-progress.md
- `color-scheme-toggle`: The dark mode control: it switches the app between light, dark and the system's scheme, and keeps the choice. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/color-scheme-toggle.md
- `page-header`: The top of a page: its title with an optional line above it (`eyebrow`), a description under it, the page's actions beside it, and a trail and an image above. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/page-header.md
- `copy-button`: A button that puts a piece of text on the clipboard: an API key, a link, a command. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/copy-button.md
- `code-block`: Code or a command on a muted surface in the theme's monospace font, with a caption and a button that copies it. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/code-block.md
- `timer`: A countdown timer with its own controls: the time left in large numbers, Start, then Pause and Cancel, Resume when paused, and at zero "Time's up" with Dismiss and Restart. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/timer.md
- `timer-tray`: The timers that are running, paused or finished, in one strip, so a person who leaves a timer's screen can still see it count down, hear it at zero, and stop it. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/timer-tray.md
- `celebrate`: A small moment of celebration for something the person finished: confetti bursts from a badge with the message ("List cleared") and screen readers hear the message once. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/celebrate.md
- `choice-card`: A set of choices shown as cards, each with a picture, a label and a line of description, for picking exactly one: a cover photo, a plan, a layout. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/choice-card.md
- `image-cropper`: A dialog for cropping a photo to a shape before it is used: drag the photo (or move it the way the arrow keys point) to choose what shows in the frame, zoom with the slider (or Plus and Minus), and Save hands the cropped image to `onCrop` as a `File`, ready for a form or an upload. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/image-cropper.md
- `image-field`: A field for one photo, shown large: the photo already saved (`src`) or the one just chosen, with Choose photo (Change photo once one shows) and Remove. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/image-field.md
- `share-button`: A button that shares a link: through the system's share sheet where there is one (phones, Safari), and by copying it where there is not, when it says "Link copied" for two seconds and screen readers hear it once. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/share-button.md
- `sync-status`: One line that says where the person's changes are: Saved, Saving…, Offline (kept on this device) or Not saved (the server refused the changes), each with its icon, and Retry while there is a problem. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/sync-status.md
- `local-date`: A date (and time) in the reader's own time zone and language, in a `<time>` that carries the exact instant. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/local-date.md
- `relative-time`: How long ago (or how soon) something happens, in the reader's language: "3 days ago", "yesterday", "in 5 minutes", "now", kept current while it shows. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/relative-time.md
- `install-prompt`: A quiet offer to install the web app, shown only where the browser can install it (Chromium on Android and desktops), never while it already runs installed, and not again for two weeks after Not now. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/install-prompt.md
- `conversation-list`: A list of conversations to choose from: each row shows the avatar, the title, when the latest message arrived and a line of it, and marks unread conversations with a bold title and a dot. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/conversation-list.md
- `attention-card`: Something that waits on the person: a mention, a question asked of them or a request still unanswered. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/attention-card.md
- `reaction-bar`: A message's reactions: each one's emoji and how many chose it, with the person's own pressed and tinted, and quick reactions to add with a single press. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/reaction-bar.md
- `lightbox`: Thumbnails that open a full-screen image viewer. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/lightbox.md
- `composer`: A chat message box: text that grows from one line as the person writes, a send button, and room for the rest of a composer, in one frame with one focus outline. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/composer.md
- `emoji-picker`: An emoji picker for reactions and for putting emoji into text. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/emoji-picker.md
- `navigation-rail`: The vertical bar of the app's top-level pages on the start edge of a wide screen, as in a chat or mail app or an editor's activity bar: each item an icon over a short label, the current one with its `currentIcon`, a bar on the rail's edge and `aria-current="page"`. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/navigation-rail.md
- `time-grid`: A day, work week or week of hours, with events placed by their times: the calendar grid of a mail or meeting app. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/time-grid.md
- `toolbar`: A row of controls for one surface, such as an editor's formatting: Button commands and Toggle states, in groups with separators. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/toolbar.md
- `agent-presence`: The person's always-visible sign of which of their agents are listening to something on their behalf, such as a meeting, with Stop one click away. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/agent-presence.md
- `autocomplete`: Suggestions at the text caret: typing a trigger character, such as `@` for people or `:` for emoji, in a `TextArea` or `TextField` opens a list beside the caret, filtered by what follows the character. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/autocomplete.md
- `emoji`: One emoji from an image catalogue, drawn as an `<img>` the size of the text around it, named by its `alt` (the emoji's name). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/emoji.md
- `level-meter`: A small live input level: a row of bars that light from the start edge as a microphone picks up sound, so the person can tell it hears them before anyone else does (before joining a call, in a device menu, in a "test your microphone" row). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/level-meter.md
- `live-captions`: A caption band for a live call or video: what people are saying, as they say it. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/live-captions.md
- `media-tile`: A tile for one live picture in a call: a person's camera, their photo when the camera is off, or a shared screen. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/media-tile.md
- `moment`: A moment in an app's life, shown in the space it is given: nothing here yet, on its way, something failed, a first run, or something finished. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/moment.md
- `snap-pip`: A floating picture inside a container, such as the person's own camera in a call, that they drag and throw into a corner, where it comes to rest, as a phone's picture in picture does. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/snap-pip.md
- `family-bar`: The slim strip above a site's own header that links every site of a family, the same links in the same order on each, after a small heading that says what it is ("Ouro family"). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/family-bar.md
- `family-footer`: The foot of a family's site: the `FamilyBar`'s links, in the same order, in a quiet row that wraps, with the site being shown marked the same way, and the site's own extras (`children`) after them. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/family-footer.md
- `hero`: The top of a page: a headline with an optional line above it (`eyebrow`) and a status beside that (`badge`), a trail above them (`breadcrumb`), a lede under the headline (`description`), the page's buttons (`actions`), more such as a byline (`children`), and a big picture, or something live in its place (`media`), below. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/hero.md
- `porthole`: The status spot: a small round window with one line about how current the app's data is, which opens into the facts behind it. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/porthole.md
- `a2ui-surface`: Shows the UI an agent composed in A2UI, with Ouro HX: it resolves the messages into core's composed tree, draws it as ComposedSurface does, its fields starting from the surface's data model, and sends a press as A2UI's action message, with what the person entered in a field a button's input is bound to. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/a2ui-surface.md
- `thread-rail`: A thread beside its conversation: a labelled landmark with a header and a close button. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/thread-rail.md
- `ouro-mcp-app`: The view an MCP server returns for agent-composed UI (MCP Apps): the host, such as Claude or ChatGPT, frames it, and it shows the latest tool result's card: Ouro's composed tree in `structuredContent.ouro` with ComposedSurface, once it passes core's `validateTree` against the catalog, its fields starting from `structuredContent.ouro.data`, or A2UI messages in `structuredContent.a2ui` with `A2UISurface`. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ouro-mcp-app.md
- `composed-surface`: Draws Ouro's composed tree with Ouro HX, whatever format it came in: core's `ComposedNode`, from A2UI messages, an MCP tool result's `structuredContent.ouro`, or your own code. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/composed-surface.md
- `unread-dot`: The dot that marks something unread: a small round dot in the theme's primary color, with a spoken label. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/unread-dot.md
- `agent-handoff`: What a person does once they have seen something built for agents: hand it to their coding agent, as one line to paste, with Copy beside it. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/agent-handoff.md
- `app-window`: A live piece of interface framed as an application's window: a title bar with a label (such as the file the demo lives in) and actions at its end, the working content inside, and the Ouro HX components it is built from along its foot. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/app-window.md
- `cover`: A thing's cover: its picture, or, without one, the first letter of its title in the theme's heading font on a solid tint of the muted color toward the primary. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/cover.md
- `section-header`: The head of a section inside a page: its title in the theme's heading font, a short count in small capitals at the end of the row (`meta`), an optional text action such as a link to the whole list, and a hairline under it. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/section-header.md
- `thread-layout`: A conversation beside its thread. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/thread-layout.md
- `chat-header`: The bar above an open chat: who it is with, and what you can do there. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/chat-header.md
- `typing-indicator`: The line under a chat that says who is writing: their faces, pulsing dots and "Ned Land is writing…". Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/typing-indicator.md
- `read-receipt`: Who has seen a message, as small faces under it: the first three readers, overlapping, then "+N" for the rest. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/read-receipt.md
- `theme-picker`: The look chooser: each look's name in its own heading face and ink, on its own paper, ending in one flat square of its primary, so the name is the specimen. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/theme-picker.md
- `page-shell`: The page column of a site: centred content with a side gutter that grows with the screen, and a wider column on big screens. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/page-shell.md
- `conversation-find`: The find bar for a conversation: a box with previous and next buttons, the match's place ("2 of 5") and a close button. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/conversation-find.md
- `freshness`: How old the data on screen is, and whether the app's cache is fetching it again: "Updated 3 minutes ago", with a small icon that turns while it refreshes. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/freshness.md
- `preview-bar`: A bar for trying a change before keeping it: the app shows a proposal live (a theme, a layout, an edit), and the bar says what it is and offers Keep, Throw away and Compare with the original. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/preview-bar.md
- `build-chip`: A compact, neutral chip for the title bar, like Xcode's scheme and activity area: it names the build the window runs ("Official 1.2.3", or "branch · sha" with "+ edits" for local changes not yet in any build), and opens a picker of the official build plus the builds serving now so a person can switch to the official build from the trigger. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/build-chip.md
- `button-tests`: Optional: the Vitest browser tests, type tests, stories and Playwright spec for button, and the tests of everything it installs. Add it beside button: add button button-tests. It names Vitest, Playwright and Storybook without a version, so the CLI installs one only when your app lacks it and never changes a version you have.

It names Vitest, Playwright and Storybook without a version, so the CLI installs one only when your app lacks it and never changes a version you have.

Add it beside freshness: add freshness freshness-tests. Add it beside preview-bar: add preview-bar preview-bar-tests. It names Vitest, Playwright and Storybook without a version, so the CLI installs one only when your app lacks it and never changes a version you have.
- `build-chip-tests`: Optional: the Vitest browser tests, type tests, stories and Playwright spec for build-chip, and the tests of everything it installs. Add it beside build-chip: add build-chip build-chip-tests. It names Vitest, Playwright and Storybook without a version, so the CLI installs one only when your app lacks it and never changes a version you have.
- `ouro-lib-tests`: Optional: the tests of every helper in lib/ouro, with ouro-lib. You don't need to add it: each -tests item installs the tests of the helpers its component imports. It names Vitest, Playwright and Storybook without a version, so the CLI installs one only when your app lacks it and never changes a version you have.
- `ouro-tests`: Optional: every Ouro UI component with its tests, type tests, stories and Playwright spec, and the test kit. The whole suite in one command. It names Vitest, Playwright and Storybook without a version, so the CLI installs one only when your app lacks it and never changes a version you have.
- `ouro-census`: Optional: the census journey kit. A Playwright spec of yours lists the pages your app renders and the states a person can open on them; the census records the exact multiset of visible controls in each (role, name, Ouro marker, context) and fails on any change from the committed baseline, and on any unmarked control in a journey you enrol. Unmarked controls may only fall, state by state. It installs e2e/ouro-census/ (the spec helper, the merge, the baseline update and a comparison of two runs).
- `ouro-source-rules`: Optional: the hand-rolled-control source rule. It reads your app's source with the TypeScript compiler and its stylesheets with PostCSS, and finds the controls still built by hand (a raw <button>, <a>, <input>, a click handler on a <div>, another UI library's control, control-state styling) and every component that wraps one, as fingerprints held to a committed baseline that may only shrink. It installs scripts/ouro-source-rules.mjs.
- `ouro-check`: Optional: the screen check. It opens every page of a built folder or a URL in headless Chromium at every screen size from 320 to 3840 wide, light and dark, and finds overlap, sideways scroll, clipped text, blurry pictures, pictures that fade into the page and serious axe-core violations, and long lines only where ouro-check.json declares a measure, and narrow text where a max-width holds prose well short of its column, each with a captioned close-up and a contact sheet per page. It measures layout shift while loading, the time to the first content and each press's time to paint, each against a budget, and records each number in its report. A run split with --shard k/n and joined with merge finds what one run does. Its fades.ts finds every gradient used as a mask in your source, and every wash laid over a picture, so no picture fades into the page. It installs scripts/ouro/check/.
- `ouro-images`: Optional: the picture sizes. It writes each raster picture in a folder as AVIF and WebP at each width up to its own, with sharp, and images.json with the srcset of each, for a <picture> element. It installs scripts/ouro/images/.
- `ouro-feel-probe`: Optional: Ouro Feel's probe, one plain script, built from feel/probe/probe.ts, that a page runs first to measure how its list feels: jumps, blank frames, late frames, input to motion and layout reads. It installs scripts/ouro/feel/ouro-feel-probe.js.
- `dashboard-page`: A page pattern: a whole dashboard page: a header with the light and dark toggle, the numbers that matter in cards, a chart of the last months and a table of recent activity.
- `list-detail-page`: A page pattern: a whole list-and-detail page: a header with the light and dark toggle, a list you can search, and the detail of the entry chosen beside it.
- `settings-page`: A page pattern: a whole settings page: a header with the light and dark toggle, a profile form the browser validates, and a danger zone that confirms before it deletes.
- `ax-bundle`: Ouro AX: A diagnostics bundle: one JSON file a doctor writes for an agent to read or attach, the agent's version of a desktop app's "get logs" menu item. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-bundle.md
- `ax-checks`: Ouro AX: A tool's checks, such as a doctor or a self-check, declared once: progress while they run, the verdict first and the results grouped for a person, the same facts as `--json` for an agent, the time taken and the exit code. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-checks.md
- `ax-claims`: Ouro AX: the Ouro AX standard as data: a claim is one checkable rule about an interface an agent uses, with the reason, the evidence that admitted it, the check `ax-xray` runs and the fix. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-claims.md
- `ax-cli`: Ouro AX: the whole front door for a tool built on the kit: parse, help, run (or, on `--dry-run`, plan), print the result as text or `--json`, and turn every failure into the one error line and its exit code. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-cli.md
- `ax-command`: Ouro AX: one definition of a command: its words, effect, arguments and flags, examples and output. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-command.md
- `ax-component`: Ouro AX: A component's agent side: what an agent may read from it and which of its actions an agent may take, each bound to the CLI command that does the same (its twin). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-component.md
- `ax-dev-commands`: Ouro AX: A message for an agent or a person names only what the installed tool runs: never a developer command, a repository path or a step that only works in a source checkout. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-dev-commands.md
- `ax-doctor`: Ouro AX: A doctor: a tool's checks (ax-checks) with the state they judged, so a person and an agent read the same facts. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-doctor.md
- `ax-effects`: Ouro AX: effect classes: a command either touches only the person's own space ("private") or reaches other people ("others"). Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-effects.md
- `ax-example`: Ouro AX: a small tool built only from the kit, the pattern to copy; the ax tests use it. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-example.md
- `ax-exit-codes`: Ouro AX: A tool's exit codes as one table: the overview, every command's footer, `help --json` and the MCP error shape read it, so the numbers never drift. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-exit-codes.md
- `ax-flows`: Ouro AX: an adopter's agent flows as data, run in CI without a model: a flow is the calls a good agent makes for one task, and the runner checks the calls' exit codes, JSON shapes and fields, error text, time, size and voice. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-flows.md
- `ax-lint`: Ouro AX: the kit's check of a tool's declarations: what an agent needs from every declared command (a summary, an example, described arguments and flags, `--why` and a preview where other people see it, help that fits the width), and, against the tool's own command inventory, that every command it registers runs through its declaration. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-lint.md
- `ax-mcp`: Ouro AX: the same definitions as an MCP server over stdio (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0), with no dependencies: one tool per command, its inputSchema from the definition, calls checked before they run with the fix in the one error shape, effects as tool annotations, and results cut to a size an agent's context can hold. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-mcp.md
- `ax-outcome`: Ouro AX: the outcome of an action: what became of it, who can see it, whether that was checked, how to find it again and what to run next, in one shape over a CLI's `--json`, an HTTP route and an MCP tool. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-outcome.md
- `ax-output`: Ouro AX: one result, two renderings: `--json` prints the data, text prints what the command's text() makes of the same data. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-output.md
- `ax-precise-copy`: Ouro AX: A failure says what happened and precisely why (the system and its answer: "The mail service says this file was deleted"), who or what caused it where that is known, and the next step as a working action. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-precise-copy.md
- `ax-probe`: Ouro AX: how a doctor tells a local process's state from outside it, so it answers whatever state the app is in: an HTTP endpoint that answers is up, one that takes the request and gives no answer in time is stuck, and one that refuses it is down. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-probe.md
- `ax-problem`: Ouro AX: one error shape for every agent surface: the CLI's stderr line, its `--json` error and an MCP tool error all carry the same fields, so an agent learns one repair loop. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-problem.md
- `ax-redact`: Ouro AX: redaction for a diagnostics bundle: what leaves the computer for an agent to read or attach keeps categories, counts, times, versions and the tool's own words, and drops tokens, cookies, ids, email addresses, paths in a person's home and what anyone wrote. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-redact.md
- `ax-surfaces`: Ouro AX: what a repository hands the checker: its agent-facing words as one JSON file a repository can produce cheaply. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-surfaces.md
- `ax-terminal`: Ouro AX: what a terminal shows a person, with a plain fallback off a terminal: colour, status marks, the time something took, next steps and a progress line for anything slow. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-terminal.md
- `ax-voice`: Ouro AX: A tool's voice: an optional line of character after the facts, for a person at a terminal, never where an agent parses. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-voice.md
- `ax-wait`: Ouro AX: A typed wait: the agent names a reference it already holds, the tool waits (polling, if it must, where the agent cannot see it) until something happens or the time limit passes, and returns what happened with the cursor that resumes the wait. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-wait.md
- `ax-work-event`: Ouro AX: an attributed work event: who acted and for whom, on what, why, with which receipt, when. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-work-event.md
- `ax-xray`: Ouro AX: the Ouro AX conformance checker: it calls a CLI, an HTTP API, an MCP server or a harness's in-turn tools the way an agent would, and reports which claims hold on which surface, with the fix where a claim does not hold. Docs: https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ax-xray.md
- `ax-bundle-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-bundle, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-checks-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-checks, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-claims-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-claims, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-cli-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-cli, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-command-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-command, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-component-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-component, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-dev-commands-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-dev-commands, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-doctor-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-doctor, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-effects-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-effects, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-exit-codes-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-exit-codes, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-flows-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-flows, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-lint-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-lint, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-mcp-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-mcp, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-outcome-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-outcome, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-output-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-output, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-precise-copy-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-precise-copy, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-probe-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-probe, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-problem-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-problem, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-redact-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-redact, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-surfaces-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-surfaces, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-terminal-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-terminal, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-voice-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-voice, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-wait-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-wait, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-work-event-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-work-event, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ax-xray-tests`: Optional: the node:test tests for ax-xray, in scripts/ouro/ax/; run them with node --test scripts/ouro/ax/*.test.mts.
- `ouro-ax`: Ouro AX, the agent-experience kit, in one item: the ax-* items, from one command definition to the X-ray that checks an interface against the claims.
- `ouro-ax-tests`: Optional: Ouro AX with the ax-* tests, the X-ray's fixtures and the example tool.
- Helpers, one item per file in lib/ouro, each installed with the components that import it (and `<name>-tests` for a helper with tests): `lib-a2ui-core`, `lib-announce`, `lib-appearance-hints`, `lib-avatar-pictures`, `lib-celebration-cap`, `lib-claims`, `lib-class-name-check`, `lib-cn`, `lib-color-scheme`, `lib-color-scheme-script`, `lib-control-ref`, `lib-css-panel`, `lib-current-path`, `lib-dev`, `lib-disabled-reason`, `lib-env`, `lib-feedback`, `lib-find-messages`, `lib-find-text`, `lib-floating`, `lib-focus-handoff`, `lib-fold-nav-placement`, `lib-fold-posture`, `lib-form-answer`, `lib-fragment-focus-script`, `lib-halve`, `lib-hero-preload-script`, `lib-insert-text`, `lib-keep-clear`, `lib-keep-focus-clear`, `lib-key-shortcuts`, `lib-last-input`, `lib-mcp-app`, `lib-measure-interaction`, `lib-navigation-key`, `lib-open-mode`, `lib-ouro-build-source`, `lib-ouro-build-source-info`, `lib-ouro-build-source-node`, `lib-ouro-provider`, `lib-page-direction`, `lib-page-scroll-hold`, `lib-people-cache`, `lib-platform`, `lib-portal-container`, `lib-porthole-view`, `lib-refs`, `lib-return-focus`, `lib-router-link`, `lib-roving-row`, `lib-row-hover`, `lib-server-element`, `lib-share`, `lib-spring`, `lib-squircle-capsules`, `lib-squircle-corners`, `lib-stretched-link`, `lib-theme-preset`, `lib-theme-preset-script`, `lib-toast`, `lib-tones`, `lib-touch-target`, `lib-use-backdrop-anchor`, `lib-use-command-shortcut`, `lib-use-counts`, `lib-use-dev-messages`, `lib-use-drag`, `lib-use-field`, `lib-use-find-highlights`, `lib-use-fold-posture`, `lib-use-install-prompt`, `lib-use-keyboard-scrollable`, `lib-use-loading-visible`, `lib-use-media-query`, `lib-use-mounted-open`, `lib-use-optimistic-action`, `lib-use-ouro`, `lib-use-person`, `lib-use-platform`, `lib-use-prefetch-intent`, `lib-use-reduced-motion`, `lib-use-sheet-presentation`, `lib-use-timer`, `lib-use-until-found`, `lib-use-view-transition`. No component imports `lib-claims`: add it by name to mark your own copy's claims with `claim()`.

## Docs

- [Docs](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/): one page per component, with props and examples. Each page is also Markdown at https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/<item>.md, the URL each item above ends with.[^docs-md]
- [Installing](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/installing.md): what ouro-base writes, what an add changes in package.json, and the "use client" notice in Vite builds.
- [Testing](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/testing.md): what the shipped tests need, Vitest 4, and how to find Ouro UI's fields in an app's own tests.[^testing-guide]
- [Forms](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/forms.md): which component shows which message, and how the controls post their values.
- [OuroProvider](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/ouro-provider.md): routing every href through the app's router, with the React Router adapter and the Next.js provider file in full.[^provider-page] It installs with every component that renders links and with tooltip; otherwise add lib-ouro-provider by name (v0.7.0 has no such item: there it comes with every component).[^provider-deps][^v0.7.0]
- [Parts](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/parts.md): the building-block parts of Sheet, Dialog and Field, for layouts the props do not cover.
- [README](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui#readme)
